officials.name: Arthur Lumpkin
officials.address: City Hall, 24 Eagle Street, Albany, NY 12207
officials.bio: Arthur L. Lumpkin is the Councilmember-elect for Albany’s 3rd Ward and a long-time resident devoted to strengthening the community he proudly calls home. A dedicated father, grandfather, and now a great grandfather, as well as a respected civic leader, Arthur has spent decades serving Albany through mentorship, hands-on neighborhood work, and public service. He currently serves as Treasurer of the Arbor Hill Development Corporation and is an active member of the Masonic family as a Prince Hall Mason, a Shriner, and a Noble.

officials.name: Deborah Zamer
officials.address: City Hall, 24 Eagle Street, Albany, NY 12207

officials.name: Deirdre Brodie
officials.address: City Hall, 24 Eagle Street, Albany, NY 12207
officials.bio: Deirdre Brodie is the Ward 6 Representative for the Common Council, bringing 20 years of residency and a successful career in government to her role. With a BA from Tufts and an MPA from the University at Albany, she has served as a Health and Human Services Policy Analyst and collaborated with numerous state and local governments. Brodie is also an active community leader, having served on multiple boards and recognized by the Albany Business Review's 40 Under 40.

officials.name: Derek Johnson
officials.address: City Hall, 24 Eagle Street, Albany, NY 12207
officials.bio: Derek A. Johnson, "DJ", grew up in Albany's South End, excelling academically and athletically before attending Saint Thomas University and Virginia Union. After returning to Albany, he joined the City School District in 1994, eventually becoming a Home School Coordinator in 2009, serving as a vital resource for Albany families and educators.

officials.name: Ginnie Farrell
officials.address: City Hall, 24 Eagle Street, Albany, NY 12207

officials.name: Jack Flynn
officials.address: City Hall, 24 Eagle Street, Albany, NY 12207
officials.bio: Jack Flynn has lived in Albany's 8th Ward for over 25 years, serving as a Committee Member and Deputy Ward Leader before becoming a Common Council Member. He previously worked in public service at the NYS Bill Drafting Commission and the Albany County Board of Elections. As a Council Member, he works with residents and leaders to ensure neighborhoods remain attractive and safe.

officials.name: John Williamson
officials.address: City Hall, 24 Eagle Street, Albany, NY 12207
officials.bio: John Williamson serves as the Common Council Member for Albany’s First Ward, making history as the first African-American man elected to represent the Ward. He brings over 30 years of service to the City of Albany through public safety, ministry, youth mentorship, and state government, having served in key roles across various institutions. Councilman Williamson is also Pastor of Heart of Love Outreach Ministries and a long-time youth coach and mentor, deeply committed to serving the First Ward and its residents.

officials.name: Lormenzo Jones
officials.address: City Hall, 24 Eagle Street, Albany, NY 12207
officials.bio: Lormenzo Jones is a proud graduate of Albany High School and served 22 years as an officer with the Albany County Sheriff's Department of Corrections. His experiences fueled a passion for community improvement, inspiring him to focus on combating food insecurity and expanding opportunities for youth and families in Albany's Fourth Ward. As a Fourth Ward resident, he is committed to being a strong and responsive voice for his neighbors, prioritizing public safety, quality of life, and affordable housing.

officials.name: Mark Robinson
officials.address: City Hall, 24 Eagle Street, Albany, NY 12207
officials.bio: Mark Robinson was born and raised in Albany, attending Albany City School District and SUNY New Paltz. He is currently serving his first term in the Albany County Legislature, representing Ward 4, and previously served one term on the Albany Common Council, championing initiatives like public transportation funding and urban street redevelopment. He is dedicated to his community, assisting seniors, distributing food, and revitalizing parks.

officials.name: Meghan Keegan
officials.address: City Hall, 24 Eagle Street, Albany, NY 12207
officials.bio: Meghan Keegan holds a Masters in Social Welfare from the University at Albany and spent 15 years working with special victims, at-risk youth, and individuals with disabilities in non-profit and state government roles. She currently works for organized labor, serves on the Executive Board for United Steel Workers Local 9265, and has been involved in various non-profit work and advocacy. Elected to the Albany Common Council in 2021 representing the 9th Ward, she has passed legislation expanding Paid Family Leave, established the Albany Commission on Disabilities, and sponsored legislation for new city departments.

officials.name: Owusu Anane
officials.address: City Hall, 24 Eagle Street, Albany, NY 12207

officials.name: Rachel Powell
officials.address: City Hall, 24 Eagle Street, Albany, NY 12207

officials.name: Sergio Adams
officials.address: City Hall, 24 Eagle Street, Albany, NY 12207
officials.bio: Sergio Adams has lived in the Capital Region for 15 years and is a graduate of the University at Albany with a degree in Urban Regional Planning. As a two-term Albany Democratic Committee member, he represents the diverse neighborhoods in the 7th Ward. Committed to making his term a transformative time for the City of Albany, Sergio focuses on affordable housing, police reform, and workforce development.

officials.name: Thomas Hoey
officials.address: City Hall, 24 Eagle Street, Albany, NY 12207

officials.name: Kelly Kimbrough
officials.address: City Hall, 24 Eagle Street, Albany, NY 12207
officials.bio: Kelly Kimbrough is a graduate of O’Neil High School and SUNY Albany, who joined the Albany Police Department in 1992, serving in various roles including Community Services Officer. He is a family man with four children and has worked to develop neighborhood watch programs and allocate resources for young people to create safer, stronger communities.

officials.name: Bryan Bollman
officials.bio: Bryan J. Bollman, a NYS Licensed Broker Associate, passionately represents his native Lovejoy District, focusing on youth well-being, job creation, and community beautification. He has secured significant funding for a mobile health clinic and Main Street Grants, demonstrating his commitment to economic development and neighborhood improvement. A University at Buffalo graduate, his work encompasses grassroots engagement, legislation, and budget planning.

officials.name: Christopher P. Scanlon
officials.bio: Christopher P. Scanlon was elected Buffalo Common Council President on January 2nd, 2024, by his Council colleagues. As Council President, he is committed to working collaboratively with all his partners in government to deliver needed resources and services to the residents of all nine council districts, and to passing legislation that supports and strengthens public safety and economic opportunity, with an emphasis on equity and inclusion.

officials.name: Leah M. Halton-Pope
officials.bio: With an extensive background in government relations at various levels and a deep-rooted commitment to public service, Halton-Pope assumed the roles of Councilwoman for the Ellicott District and Majority Leader for the Buffalo Common Council in January 2024. Her appointment marks a new chapter for the district, one characterized by inclusivity, progress, and unwavering dedication to the community.

officials.bio: Cathlin B. Gleason serves as the Acting President Pro Tem for the City Council.

officials.name: Derrick Thompson
officials.bio: Councilman Derrick Thompson is a Mount Vernon native and a product of its school district. He holds bachelor's and master's degrees from Mercy College and began his career at the Mount Vernon School District in 1995. He is dedicated to serving his community, uplifting, encouraging, and teaching people, and has been on the front lines ensuring residents were taken care of during the Covid-19 pandemic.

officials.name: André Wallace
officials.bio: Mr. Wallace started his career in entertainment and music, then shifted to building and design as president and owner of Creative Direction Construction & Design. He later discovered a passion for serving others, leading him to public office where he served as a City Councilman and President of the City Council.

officials.name: Cynthia Turnquest - Jones
officials.bio: Cynthia Turnquest-Jones was elected to the Mt. Vernon City Council in November 2025, bringing over 57 years of residency and a lifelong commitment to service. She has a strong background from 29 years with the NYC Department of Education in leadership roles and is committed to advancing safer streets, stronger schools, and cleaner neighborhoods. She also founded Let Girls Learn Days and is an active member of Moms Demand Action.

officials.name: Jaevon Boxhill
officials.bio: Jaevon Boxhill is the President Pro Tem of the City Council and a Mount Vernon City Councilman for 2024.

officials.name: William B. Namestnik
officials.bio: William B. Namestnik is the Hopewell Town Supervisor and Vice-Chair of the Board. He was elected in 2022 for a 1-year term and serves on the Governmental Operations and Insurance, and Public Safety Standing Committees.

officials.name: Kevin M. Byrne
officials.bio: “Remember that Putnam County is home. Regardless of what may make us different as individuals, it is our respect for each-other as neighbors, our desire to step up and serve, to lend a hand, and leave this beautiful county better off than we found it. That is what makes this place so special. It is with that in mind that we as a county government are here to serve, and will always serve, with a desire to do better.” - Kevin M. Byrne | Putnam County Executive

officials.name: Malik D. Evans
officials.bio: Malik D. Evans is the City of Rochester’s 71st Mayor. He is committed to creating a safe, equitable and prosperous Rochester by inspiring hope and delivering opportunity for everyone. Inaugurated on Jan. 1, 2022, Mayor Evans has governed with a commitment to transparency and collaboration, concisely captured by his working mantra “It’s we, not me.”

officials.bio: Amy Dooley represents District No. 9, which includes the Town of Esopus and the Town of Lloyd.

officials.name: Dominick Marino
officials.bio: Dominick Marino serves as the Ulster County Legislator for District 10, representing Highland and Marlborough. A dedicated advocate for mental health, housing stability, and community well-being, Dominick brings years of professional and lived experience to his role in county government.

officials.name: Laura Donovan
officials.bio: Laura Donovan represents District 11 in the Ulster County Legislature, serving the communities of Milton and Marlboro. A lifelong advocate for families and community well-being, she brings a decade of experience in financial planning, small-business engagement, and nonprofit leadership to her role in county government.

officials.name: Lindsey Grossman
officials.bio: Lindsey Grossman, a leader in technology, small business growth, and public health, serves as the Ulster County Legislator representing District 19 (Town of Rosendale and Town of Marbletown). As Legislator, Lindsey works to advance affordable housing, economic development, and environmental protection. She brings global and local leadership experience across public and private sectors and serves her community with empathy, energy, and expertise.

officials.name: Michael Berardi
officials.bio: Beginning his third term as an Ulster County Legislator, Michael Berardi has broad governmental experience, including four years on the Ulster Town Board and as Chairperson of The Ulster County Industrial Development Agency. With a lifetime of experience in the Energy sector, he is currently employed by HOP Energy KOSCO Heritagenergy Kingston. He is married with two children and four grandchildren, and has served the community as a Rhinebeck Rotarian and on the Board of Anderson School.

officials.name: William Murray
officials.bio: William Murray is a twice-elected New Paltz Village Trustee and dedicated interior volunteer firefighter, honored twice as Firefighter of the Year. He has served nine years on the Ulster County Planning Board and acted as the Village Board liaison for several committees, including the New Paltz Planning Board, Bicycle Pedestrian Committee and Historic Preservation Commission.
